title: When Team Members Openly Disrespect Each Other
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece separates a team member's private doubts about a colleague's competence or character from the public display of disrespect, arguing leaders should focus on stopping the latter rather than trying to change the former. It notes that beliefs about a colleague are hard to shift once cemented, but leaders must insist those beliefs never surface as observable disrespect in team settings. The piece endorses one of the rare moments where public confrontation of behavior is appropriate, offering a sample line leaders can use in the moment. It closes by warning that a leader's silence in the face of disrespect is read by the team as agreement, which compounds the damage.
points: Private doubts about a colleague's skill or character are distinct from public displays of disrespect.
Changing entrenched beliefs about a colleague is described as difficult and often unsuccessful.
Leaders should draw a hard line: beliefs can remain private, but disrespect must never be displayed openly.
This is one of the rare situations where public, in-the-moment confrontation is appropriate.
A leader's silence when disrespect occurs is read by the team as tacit agreement.
quotes: Disrespect between team members can severely change how the larger team interacts.
Any time leaders observe or sense disrespect, so do other team members.
That comment crossed the line. We don't speak to each other that way here.
Silence from the leader in the moment is typically read as agreement.
They may not be able to change the beliefs of team members about each other, but they can insist on professional protocol in each and every team discussion.
